title: Government Strengthens Monitoring of Funds Earmarked for Welfare and Development of Scheduled Castes under DAPSC
subtitle: 38 Ministries/Departments Earmarking Funds under Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes; Periodic Reviews Undertaken to Ensure Optimal Utilisation
body_text:
The Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that, as per the NITI Aayog Guidelines, 2017 for the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), earlier known as the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), 38 Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are earmarking funds across various schemes for the welfare and development of Scheduled Castes.
Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale shared these details in reply to Questions asked by SHRI GOLLA BABURAO in Rajya Sabha regarding the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes.
The data on Budget Estimates (BE), Revised Estimates (RE) and actual expenditure under DAPSC across Ministries/Departments since 2020-21 shows that actual expenditure remained below the Revised Estimates during each of the years from 2020-21 to 2025-26. The utilisation of Revised Estimates was 81.61 per cent in 2020-21, 91.22 per cent in 2021-22, 91.90 per cent in 2022-23, 93.83 per cent in 2023-24, 92.57 per cent in 2024-25 and 85.65 per cent in 2025-26 .
The Government stated that the funds are earmarked only for the welfare of Scheduled Castes. However, due to the general nature of schemes in some Ministries/Departments, the funds are not utilised fully in certain cases.
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment oversees the utilisation of DAPSC funds by the obligated Ministries/Departments through periodic review meetings under the chairpersonship of the Hon’ble Minister and Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment. In the recent past, review meetings under DAPSC were held under the chairpersonship of Shri B.L. Verma, Hon’ble Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, on April 29, 2025 , and at the level of Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment on August 25, 2025 and April 16, 2026 .
From time to time, through communications, DAPSC-obligated Ministries/Departments are asked to expedite expenditure and ensure optimal utilisation of funds earmarked under DAPSC . Further, in adherence to the directions issued by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, all 38 Ministries/Departments implementing DAPSC have nominated a nodal officer for financial and physical monitoring of DAPSC funds in their respective Ministries/Departments.
The Government continues to strengthen monitoring and review mechanisms to ensure optimal utilisation of funds earmarked under DAPSC for the welfare and development of Scheduled Castes.

enrichment.summary: The Government told the Rajya Sabha that 38 Ministries/Departments earmark funds under the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), formerly the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), as per NITI Aayog's 2017 guidelines. Data since 2020-21 shows actual expenditure has consistently fallen short of Revised Estimates, with utilisation ranging from 81.61% (2020-21) to a peak of 93.83% (2023-24), and 85.65% in 2025-26. The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment monitors fund utilisation through periodic review meetings and has directed all 38 ministries to appoint nodal officers for financial and physical monitoring of DAPSC funds.
enrichment.context:
DAPSC (earlier SCSP) is a budgetary mechanism requiring Union ministries to earmark funds proportionate to the Scheduled Caste population for schemes benefiting SC communities, aiming to bridge the socio-economic gap between SCs and the general population. It parallels the Tribal Sub-Plan (now Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes) for STs. Since its inception, the scheme has faced criticism for diversion of funds, underutilisation, and 'notional' earmarking where general schemes are counted without SC-specific outcomes—issues reflected in the consistent shortfall between Revised Estimates and actual expenditure reported here. NITI Aayog's 2017 guidelines sought to strengthen the framework by mandating monitoring, but implementation gaps persist due to the generic nature of some schemes not being tailored to SC beneficiaries.

This periodic parliamentary reporting is part of a broader accountability mechanism for social sector spending, relevant to India's constitutional commitment under Articles 15(4), 16(4A), and 46 to promote the welfare of SCs. Persistent underutilisation of earmarked funds has implications for the effectiveness of affirmative action and targeted welfare delivery, a recurring theme in the Standing Committee reports and CAG audits on scheduled caste welfare expenditure.

prelims_questions.question: The Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC), mentioned in news, was earlier known by which name?
prelims_questions.explanation: DAPSC was earlier known as the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP), renamed and reformed as per NITI Aayog Guidelines, 2017.

prelims_questions.question: As per NITI Aayog Guidelines, 2017, how many Ministries/Departments of the Government of India earmark funds under DAPSC?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states that 38 Ministries/Departments of the Government of India are earmarking funds under DAPSC as per NITI Aayog Guidelines, 2017.

mains_questions.question: Examine the objectives of the Development Action Plan for Scheduled Castes (DAPSC). Discuss the challenges in fund utilisation under this plan and suggest measures to improve its effectiveness in achieving socio-economic upliftment of Scheduled Castes.

Earmarking of funds for vulnerable sections such as Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is often criticised for being merely notional rather than outcome-oriented. Critically analyse this observation in the context of DAPSC/DAPST implementation in India.
